key_insight: Optical-fiber daylighting can cut vertical-farm lighting electricity use substantially, but today’s fiber costs keep it economically unattractive.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that sunlight delivery to crop shelves can meaningfully reduce LED dependence, but only if optical efficiency, heat management, and capital cost are improved.
method: Coupled a validated transient vertical-farm model with Tonatiuh ray tracing for a single-axis tracked Fresnel concentrator.
Compared five optical-fiber types and three daylighting strategies against light-pipe and rooftop PV baselines.
Evaluated useful-PAR delivery, crop production, specific electrical energy consumption, and light cost.
evidence_signal: The optical-fiber system delivered 19–27% annual useful-PAR efficiency and reduced electricity use by 35–89%, while hybrid strategies reached about 50% savings with minimum SEEC of 3.16 kWh kg^-1.
watch_item: Despite strong energy savings, the system needs about a 90% capital-cost reduction to be competitive, so near-term deployment is limited by fiber cost.
paper_title: Can sunlight replace LEDs in vertical farms? A critical assessment of optical-fiber daylighting strategies
